summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ , a man with secondary progressive multiple sclerosis and neurogenic bladder managed with a chronic Foley catheter, was admitted with acute right arm weakness and general malaise. Evaluation revealed a urinary tract infection with E. coli resistant to trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole but sensitive to ampicillin/sulbactam. He was treated with intravenous Unasyn and transitioned to oral Augmentin. His neurological symptoms improved with infection treatment. A Foley catheter change resolved associated hematuria. He was discharged home with services, instructions to complete antibiotics, discontinue Bactrim and methenamine hippurate temporarily, and follow up with urology and MS infusion clinic.
